subject: Re: Prompt set collection + recommended models / benchmarks (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prompt set collection + recommended models / benchmarks (Acme)

Hi John —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Model recommendations: based on the examples you shared and the latency targets (<= 300ms p95) we typically recommend starting with: 
   - redwood-7b-optim (dense, FP16) for baseline accuracy/latency tradeoff
   - redwood-13b-quant (8-bit) for higher-quality responses if you can accept slightly higher tail latency
   - a smaller distilled variant for bursty, low-cost routing on lower-priority traffic

   I’ve attached our internal benchmark summary for these variants and a short note on quantization impact.

2) Eval / benchmark links: I’ll drop the shared Drive folder with our example prompt sets and scoring rubric after this thread. Expect: latency/throughput CSVs, BLEU/ROUGE-like automated metrics where applicable, and a human-eval sheet for subjective categories (intent matching, hallucination, safety).

3) Prompt set collection: Can you upload a representative sample of customer prompts (50–200 examples to start) including: happy path prompts, edge cases, and a handful of redaction-sensitive examples (PII / account numbers) so we can validate our redaction guidance? Please keep PII in a separate column and mark which fields need redaction.

4) Security/redaction guidance: We can provide a one-page redaction checklist. We recommend removing full account numbers and replacing with tokenized placeholders (e.g., <ACCOUNT_ID>). If you need, we can apply a sample redaction pass and return a redacted CSV for your review.

5) Timeline / next steps:
   - You: upload prompt CSV + brief note on edge cases by EOD Thu (2026-07-23)
   - Us: run initial model-fit evals and share results + recommended config by Tue (2026-07-28)

Attachments: acme_prompt_template.csv (template), benchmark_overview.pdf

If that looks good, we’ll proceed with the eval run and set up a short sync to review results.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
From: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>

Cc: legal@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-07-20T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection + recommended models / benchmarks (Acme)

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. I’m attaching a first pass: acme_prompts_v1.csv. It contains ~120 rows broken into customer_inquiry, desired_output, and a PII column (account_number). A few notes: 

- Edge cases: multi-intent requests, malformed JSON blobs in inputs, and legacy product codes that sometimes look like account numbers.
- Redaction: we can’t share full account numbers externally; the PII column contains masked tokens for rows we’re allowed to share. Where masked, we include a boolean flag shareable=true.
- Stakeholders: looping in Legal for confirmation on data handling (legal@acmecorp.com).

We expect to have another 200 prompts from Support next week — I’ll upload in the same CSV format if this works.

Thanks,
John
Director, Product Ops
Acme Corp
john.doe@acmecorp.com

Attachments: acme_prompts_v1.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection + recommended models / benchmarks (Acme)

Thanks John — this is perfect and exactly what we need to get started. A few quick clarifications: 

- For rows where account_number is masked, the boolean shareable=true is sufficient for our eval; if you’re able to provide one or two fully synthetic-but-structured examples (fake numbers matching the same format) that’d help validate redaction rules without exposing real PII.
- Edge cases: please flag rows with legacy product codes in a separate column named legacy_flag so we can group them during eval.
- Consent: Legal, if you’re ok with the masked CSV plus synthetic examples, we’ll proceed. We’ll also provide a redaction checklist PDF (privacy_redaction_guidance.pdf) and can run a redaction pass before anything leaves your environment.

David — looping you in to coordinate the eval cadence and confirm we have the right compute profile for the 13B quant runs (we may recommend a dedicated slot for stable comparisons).

Will start the initial tagging scripts on our side once the upload is in the Drive link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cacme-eval-sets

Best,
Marissa

- I’ve provisioned a 13B quant eval slot for ACME on our dedicated infra for the 7/28 run.

John — if you prefer, I can send the NDA + rubric to legal@acmecorp.com.
